spec_location: §4.6 verification table, row at line 203; DoD line 336
claim: "| Reduced motion removes movement, not function | emulate `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, re-run the state pass, assert the element still reaches its end state |" — under the rule at line 189: "**Named tooling per check.** Every row names its mechanism; a check whose mechanism is unavailable is recorded **`UNVERIFIABLE`**, never `PASS`."

The Playwright MCP surface the proposal targets exposes no media-emulation tool at all. The single route is `browser_run_code_unsafe`, which reaches `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` in the Playwright *server* process — a tool the proposal never names, no Belmont agent references, and whose own description flags it as RCE-equivalent. spec_location: §4.6 verification table, row at line 197; severity ladder at line 211

On such an install neither the contract nor the preview ever reaches a commit — durability still holds (the copy paths are filesystem-based, not git-based) but the reviewability argument, which is one of the two stated reasons for choosing this placement, silently does not apply. The proposal states the diff claim unconditionally.
